subject: Physics
description: Conductors / insulators / semiconductors, doping, p-n junction, diodes

questions.explanation: SEMICONDUCTOR — material with conductivity BETWEEN good conductors (Cu, Ag) and good insulators (glass, rubber). Examples: Silicon (Si), Germanium (Ge), GaAs. Energy band gap small (~1.1 eV for Si). Conductivity INCREASES with temperature (opposite to metals — hence 'negative temperature coefficient of resistance'). Adding impurities (DOPING) can drastically change conductivity. Foundation of electronics — diodes, transistors, ICs, solar cells, LEDs all built from semiconductors.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Adding small amounts of impurities to a pure semiconductor (DOPING) is done to:

options.option_text: Convert it into an insulator type

questions.explanation: Pure semiconductor (intrinsic Si) — low conductivity. DOPING (~1 part per million) → boosts conductivity by ORDERS of magnitude. Two types: N-TYPE — dope with PENTAVALENT atom (P, As, Sb): 5 valence electrons; 4 bond, 1 free → extra ELECTRONS; e is majority carrier. P-TYPE — dope with TRIVALENT atom (B, Al, Ga, In): 3 valence electrons → leaves a 'HOLE' (missing electron); hole is majority carrier. Combining n + p → P-N JUNCTION = the basic DIODE.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A P-N JUNCTION DIODE allows current to flow:

options.option_text: Only when reverse-biased always at all
Equally well in both directions of bias
Only when there is no applied voltage

questions.explanation: DIODE — one-way valve for current. FORWARD BIAS: p-side connected to + terminal, n-side to − terminal → low resistance, current flows easily. REVERSE BIAS: p to −, n to + → very high resistance, almost no current. (At very high reverse voltage, breakdown occurs — Zener / avalanche.) Used as RECTIFIER (AC → DC). Half-wave (1 diode) + full-wave (4 diodes in bridge) rectifiers. Diode symbol: triangle pointing toward bar.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: An LED (Light-Emitting Diode) emits light when:

options.option_text: Lit by sunlight on its outer surface

questions.explanation: LED — special diode. When FORWARD-BIASED, electrons + holes recombine at the junction; energy released as PHOTONS (light). Colour depends on semiconductor's BAND GAP: red = GaAsP, green = GaP, blue = InGaN, white = blue LED + yellow phosphor (or 3-LED mix). Inventors of efficient blue LED — Akasaki, Amano, Nakamura (Nobel 2014). Why LED is replacing incandescent: ~10× more efficient (no heat loss), longer life, lower cost. Indian UJALA scheme (2015) sold ~370 million LEDs at low price, big energy saver.

questions.stem: The TRANSISTOR was invented in 1947 at:
questions.explanation: TRANSISTOR — invented at BELL LABS (USA), Dec 1947, by John BARDEEN, Walter BRATTAIN, William SHOCKLEY. Nobel Prize 1956. Replaced vacuum tubes — smaller, cheaper, more reliable, much less power. Started the electronics revolution. Transistor types: BJT (Bipolar Junction — n-p-n or p-n-p), FET (Field-Effect), MOSFET (Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor FET — used in modern ICs). Modern CPU has BILLIONS of MOSFETs (e.g., Apple M-series chip: ~50-100 billion transistors). MOORE'S LAW — transistor count doubles every ~2 years (slowing now).
questions.subject: Physics

options.option_text: Chemical energy into electricity from cells

questions.explanation: SOLAR CELL (photovoltaic cell, PV) — converts LIGHT directly into electricity using PHOTOELECTRIC effect. Made of doped silicon (p-n junction). Sunlight photons free electrons; junction's electric field separates them → current flows. Efficiency: typical Si cells ~15-22%. Theoretical max for single junction ~33% (Shockley-Queisser limit). Solar Mission of India: 100 GW solar by 2022 (target met partly), now aiming 500 GW by 2030. Bhadla Solar Park (Rajasthan) — among world's largest. Distractor 1 = thermoelectric. Distractor 4 = battery.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Common P-type DOPANT for silicon (adding 'holes' to it) is:
questions.explanation: P-TYPE doping: add TRIVALENT atoms (3 valence electrons) like BORON (B), Aluminium (Al), Gallium (Ga), Indium (In). Creates 'HOLES' — missing electrons that act like positive charge carriers. N-TYPE doping: add PENTAVALENT atoms (5 valence electrons) like PHOSPHORUS (P), Arsenic (As), Antimony (Sb). Provides extra free electrons (n-type carriers). Distractor 1 (P) = N-type. Distractor 3 (C) = same valence as Si, doesn't make donor or acceptor. Distractor 4 (O) = doesn't dope semiconductors usefully.
